charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentMix.title: Revenue mix: Data Center vs Communications & Other
segmentMix.content:
Marvell discloses two end markets: Data Center (AI/cloud custom silicon, switching, interconnect, storage) and Communications & Other (enterprise networking, carrier infrastructure, consumer, automotive/industrial combined).

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: this is the core investment thesis -- Data Center was 40% of revenue in FY2024 and has risen past ~79% by Q2 FY2027, almost entirely on AI custom-silicon programs with hyperscale customers. Communications & Other is not necessarily shrinking in dollars, it is simply being outgrown.

What to watch:

  • Whether Data Center growth keeps outrunning Communications & Other, or whether the mix stabilises
  • Customer-program concentration within Data Center (see the concentration chart) -- the mix shift and the customer-concentration shift are the same underlying story

legacySegments.title: Communications & Other: legacy sub-segments
legacySegments.content:
Before Q4 FY2026, Marvell reported Communications & Other as four separate segments: enterprise networking, carrier infrastructure, consumer and automotive/industrial. These four summed exactly to the Communications & Other total shown in the mix chart above.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: all four were flat-to-declining through FY2025 (carrier infrastructure fell from $1,084m in FY2023 to $338m in FY2025), which is why management stopped breaking them out -- and why the automotive ethernet business was sold to Infineon for $2.5bn in August 2025.

What to watch:

  • This chart is history only -- it goes blank after Q3 FY2026 because the data is no longer disclosed, not because the business stopped
  • Don't sum this chart against the mix chart above for post-FY2026 periods -- the detail isn't there any more

customerConcentration.title: Top-10 customer revenue concentration
customerConcentration.content:
Share of total revenue from Marvell's ten largest customers, disclosed annually.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: concentration has risen alongside the Data Center mix shift -- 72% in FY2024 to 82% in FY2026 -- because AI custom-silicon revenue is lumpy and program-specific, tied to a handful of hyperscale customers (concentration risk the Data Center growth story carries with it).

What to watch:

  • A single customer's capex pause or program loss now moves the whole top line far more than it would in a diversified semiconductor business
  • FY-only: disclosed annually, not quarterly

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Marvell Technology, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
